definition: The minimum energy that colliding particles need for a successful collision that leads to a reaction; on an energy profile it is the rise from the reactants to the top of the hump.

A graph of how the kinetic energies of the particles in a sample are spread out at one temperature: it starts at the origin, peaks at the most likely energy and tails off towards the energy axis without touching it, and its area stands for the total number of particles.
A substance that increases the rate of a reaction by providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy and is not used up; it changes neither $\Delta H$ nor the position of equilibrium.
